6 teams from the interior | matches = 382 | total goals = 1012 | average goals = 2.65 | prevseason = [[1993 Paraguayan Primera División season|1993]] | nextseason = [[1995 Paraguayan Primera División season|1995]] }} The '''1994 Paraguayan [[Paraguayan Primera División|Primera División]] Championship''' was the 84th season of the [[Primera División de Paraguay]], the top-flight football league in [[Paraguay]], organized by the [[Paraguayan Football Association|Paraguayan Football League]] (LPF). In the end, [[Cerro Porteño]] won their 23rd national title by defeating [[Olimpia Asunción|Olimpia]] in the final match.{{cite web |url=http://www.rsssf.com/tablesp/parachamp.html |title=Paraguay - List of Champions and Runners Up |author=Juan Pablo Andrés and Osvaldo José |publisher=RSSSF |access-date=21 April 2025}} == Competition system == The tournament was played in two stages using a [[round-robin tournament|single round-robin format]], meaning each team played 19 matches. The winners of each stage faced each other in a final to determine the overall champion.{{cite web |url=http://www.rsssf.com/tablesp/para94.html |title=Paraguay 1994 |author=RSSSF |publisher=Enda Mulcahy |language=English |access-date=21 April 2025}} Due to a reform in the championship structure, six teams from outside the capital were included in the tournament. {{reflist|group="n"|refs= Pettirossi and Guaraní from Coronel Oviedo finished the tournament tied in last place, so they played a playoff match to determine which team would be relegated. Pettirossi won 3–1, resulting in the relegation of Guaraní from Coronel Oviedo to their regional league.}} {| style="margin:1em auto;" |- |bgcolor=#E9967A style="border: 1px solid black"| |bgcolor=#ffffff|Relegated to regional league. |} === Additional relegations === Due to a structural reorganization of the tournament, teams that did not belong to the [[Gran Asunción|metropolitan area of Asunción]] were excluded from the following championship, and thus the five remaining clubs from the countryside were returned to their respective regional leagues. In addition, [[Club River Plate|River Plate]] and [[Club Sportivo Trinidense|Sportivo Trinidense]] were relegated to the [[Paraguayan División Intermedia|Second Division]] as they were the two lowest-ranked teams from the metropolitan area based on accumulated points. == References == {{Reflist}} [[Category:1994 in South American football leagues]] [[Category:Paraguayan Primera División seasons]]
